title: Adding Floors to an Old House: Structure, Foundation and Permit Checks
desc: Adding floors to an old house: how to check the foundation and structure, whether a repair and renovation permit is needed, the file contents and key risks.
summary: What to do before adding floors to an old house: survey, structural and foundation assessment, renovation design, and a repair and renovation permit under the Construction Law 2025.
body: p

Adding floors is a way to increase living area without buying new land. But an old house was designed for its original number of floors; adding a floor means adding load onto the columns, beams and foundation. Doing it wrongly can cause settlement and cracks, and even endanger both your house and the neighboring one.
h2
1. The first question: can the foundation and structure bear it?
p

This cannot be answered by experience or by eye. A survey of the existing condition is needed: the type of foundation, the size and quality of columns, beams and slabs, the concrete strength, the condition of the reinforcement, and the history of settlement and cracks. Ideally the original design drawings and old as-built completion drawings (hoàn công) are still kept. On that basis, a structural engineer calculates whether floors can be added, how many, and whether the foundation or columns must be strengthened first.
ul
A house built on weak ground that already shows signs of settlement or tilting is usually hard to add floors to without strengthening the foundation.
A load-bearing brick-wall house (with no concrete frame) usually has limited ability to add floors.
The load can be reduced with a light structure for the new floor (steel frame, light slab) – but it must still be calculated.
h2
2. Who does the renovation design?
p

Under Clause 2, Article 10 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP, a homeowner may organize the design themselves only when the house simultaneously has fewer than 3 floors, no basement, a total floor area under 250 m² and a height under 12 m. After adding floors, most houses will exceed these thresholds, so the design must be carried out by a qualified, experienced organization or individual. If the use is changed (for example, a business floor) together with renovation, the design and construction must suit the new use (Clause 5, Article 10).
h2
3. Is a permit required to add floors?
p

The Construction Law 2025 has a type of permit for repair, renovation and relocation of works (Clause 1, Article 43). A permit is waived only when the repair or renovation is inside the building, or on an exterior that does not adjoin an urban street subject to architectural management requirements, while not affecting the safety of the load-bearing structure and not changing the use (Point h, Clause 2, Article 43). Adding floors changes the load-bearing structure and the height of the house, so it does not fall under this waiver; if the house is exempt from a new-construction permit under Point g (houses under 7 floors and under 500 m² of floor area, outside the planned areas listed in the law), it must be rechecked whether it still qualifies after the floors are added.
p

Conditions for granting a repair and renovation permit under Article 51 of Decree 217/2026/ND-CP: it must meet the conditions for a new-construction permit in Clauses 1–4 of Article 50 (including conformity with planning – that is, the number of floors and height after the addition must be allowed by the planning).
h2
4. Application file for a repair and renovation permit
p
Under Article 61 of Decree 217/2026/ND-CP, the file includes:
ol
An application for a repair and renovation permit in Form No. 01 of Appendix II to Decree 217/2026/ND-CP;
One of the valid land documents under Article 55;

Drawings of the existing condition of the parts of the building planned for repair and renovation, and photographs (at least 10 x 15 cm) of the existing condition of the building and neighboring buildings before the renovation;
The repair and renovation design file corresponding to the type of building.
p

The procedure, place of submission and processing time are similar to a permit for a detached house – see the article on the procedure for a detached house construction permit 2026. Renovating without a permit or contrary to the permit may result in penalties and an order to demolish the violating part (penalties for building without a permit or contrary to a permit).
h2
5. During construction of the added floors
ul
Provide support measures to keep adjoining houses safe; take photos and prepare a record of the neighbor's existing condition before starting.
Check the connection between old and new structure (columns, starter bars) exactly as designed.
Review the electrical, water supply and drainage systems and the old roof waterproofing; the old roof becomes a floor, so the waterproofing must be redone.

When finished, update the as-built file to carry out the procedure to record the changes on the title certificate (as-built completion and registering the house on the land use right certificate (sổ đỏ)).
p

note

This article is for reference; whether each house can have floors added must be surveyed and calculated by a qualified person. Regulations are cited under Construction Law 135/2025/QH15, Decree 207/2026/ND-CP and 217/2026/ND-CP (in force; Article 74 of Decree 217/2026/ND-CP has been repealed and is not relevant to the content of this article).
